headline: Anthropic founders cash out nearly $2B in record IPO
dek: TechCrunch and Fortune report each of the seven sold shares and took home about $280 million before taxes.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: Seven founders, one sale
body: Each of the seven co-founders sold about 3.4 million shares and took home roughly $280 million before fees and taxes (TechCrunch, Fortune).
Together the founders cashed out about $1.95 billion, according to TechCrunch.

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: Who controls the company
s3.body: Despite a minority stake, the founders stay in charge.

points.t: The founders keep 50.1% of voting power (Fortune).
Amazon and Google end up with 28% of the company (TechCrunch, Fortune).
They pledged 80% of their equity to philanthropy, not legally binding (Fortune).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Largest IPO ever recorded
body: Anthropic raised $81.3 billion on Nasdaq, topping SpaceX's record, according to Wired.
The post-offering valuation is about $1.5 trillion (Wired).

stat.cap: raised on Nasdaq, an IPO record (Wired)

items.t: Nvidia and Google each bought $10 billion in non-voting shares (TechCrunch).
An almost even split among the seven is unusual in Silicon Valley (Fortune).

caption.hook: Anthropic's founders cash out nearly $2B in the largest IPO ever.
body: Each of the seven co-founders sold about 3.4 million shares and took home roughly $280 million before taxes, according to TechCrunch and Fortune. Altogether that is about $1.95 billion (TechCrunch). They pledged 80% of their remaining equity to philanthropy, though the pledge is not legally binding (Fortune).

Despite a minority stake, the founders keep 50.1% of voting power (Fortune). The offering raised $81.3 billion on Nasdaq, the largest IPO on record (Wired), and Amazon and Google end up with a combined 28% of the company (TechCrunch, Fortune).
caption.cta: Is a founder-controlled AI giant good or risky for the industry?
